JVA is a micro-cap speculative shadow for wholesale/private-label coffee and direct foodservice channels; require confirmation that foodservice/private-label exposure is material and profitable.

Public pure-play exposure is thin because several relevant coffee/private-label suppliers are private or recently taken private, including TreeHouse Foods; later searches should map private competitors only as context, not candidates.

WEST is the highest-priority underfollowed candidate for the coffee/tea/extract/private-label foodservice node because filings directly tie it to foodservice and restaurant customers plus extract and RTD capacity.

FARM is a high-relevance but high-risk speculative shadow candidate: filings support DSD, equipment service, and restaurant/foodservice customers, but market cap and turnaround risk place it below the preferred size threshold.

HBB is a below-$300M speculative equipment candidate whose commercial restaurant, fast-food, bar, hotel, coffee maker, and specialty beverage equipment exposure needs revenue-materiality verification.

For this node, the most Serenity-relevant chokepoints appear to be extraction/RTD capacity, green-coffee sourcing and commodity management, direct-store-delivery route density, equipment service uptime, and customer-specific beverage formulation.
Need a separate pass for private-label beverage and tea manufacturers such as TreeHouse Foods if it remains publicly listed and sufficiently exposed after any take-private or portfolio changes.

WEST is the highest-priority public small-cap candidate for the coffee/tea/extract/private-label foodservice supply node because filings directly mention foodservice and restaurant customers plus extract, RTD, sourcing, roasting, packaging and distribution capabilities.

FARM is a direct node match through DSD coffee/tea, foodservice customers and equipment service, but should be treated as a speculative shadow candidate due to micro-cap size, losses, leverage/liquidity risk and need to verify route economics.

JVA is a micro-cap speculative exception with wholesale green coffee, private-label and foodservice exposure; include only if later layers can verify material foodservice/customer-chain exposure and manageable commodity/customer concentration risk.

MIDD is not coffee-pure, but provides a mid-cap public route into coffee/beverage equipment and service exposure through commercial foodservice equipment brands; later work must size the coffee/beverage contribution.

TreeHouse Foods was removed from the candidate list because it completed a take-private transaction in February 2026. Its acquisition is still useful as a market signal that private-label food and beverage manufacturing assets remain strategically valuable.

The node’s likely chokepoints are not consumer-facing restaurant brands but B2B formulation, extract/RTD capacity, traceable sourcing, DSD route density, coffee equipment uptime and customer-specific private-label programs.

WEST should remain a priority Layer 2 diligence candidate for the coffee/tea/extract/private-label beverage node, but only if filings confirm foodservice/customer exposure, utilization, margin path, and manageable leverage.

THS may be a second-order private-label coffee/beverage supplier through acquired Farmer Brothers assets, but restaurant and foodservice exposure must be verified before promotion beyond hypothesis/inference status.

Need filing-level search for direct restaurant or foodservice customer exposure across coffee/extract suppliers, including customer concentration, named customer references, channel revenue, and commodity pass-through mechanisms.
